candidate_relations.reason: AML with maturation is a related acute myeloid leukemia with incompatible lineage from mast-cell leukaemia.
Myelodysplastic syndrome captures trilineage dysplasia but not mast-cell leukaemia.
Myeloproliferative neoplasm is a parent myeloid category missing mast-cell leukaemia.
Acute myeloid leukemia is a related blast leukemia but a different WHO entity from mast-cell leukaemia.
Systemic lupus erythematosus does not explain metachromatic marrow blasts.
Acute promyelocytic leukemia can share bilobed granular blasts but is a different PML-RARA disease.
Juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia is an incompatible age/entity.
Histiocytosis is a broad histiocytic parent related to erythrophagocytosis, not mast-cell leukaemia.
Subacute histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis does not explain circulating metachromatic blasts.
Systemic mastocytosis is the parent mast-cell neoplasm missing the leukaemic MCL variant.
Tuberculosis is a remote treated infection, not the acute leukemia.
Hairy-cell leukemia is a different chronic B-cell leukemia.
Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis describes the hyperferritin/erythrophagocytosis syndrome accompanying the leukemia.
Histiocytic medullary reticulosis is a historical HLH-like label, not mast-cell leukaemia.
TTP does not fit metachromatic blasts and massive splenomegaly with infarction.
Langerhans cell histiocytosis is a different histiocytic neoplasm.
Lymphoma is a related hematologic malignancy of incompatible lineage.
Chronic myelomonocytic leukemia is a different myeloid neoplasm.
Disseminated intravascular coagulation may accompany cytopenias and bleeding but is not mast-cell leukaemia.
Histiocytic sarcoma is a different aggressive histiocytic malignancy.

case_quality_flags: No complete_equivalent candidate; mast cell leukaemia is not named
Ferritin >40000 and erythrophagocytosis raise an HLH-overlap phenotype around the mast-cell leukemia
